newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: CLT-UFA sees 100 bln Luxfr turnover in 1997.
newsitem.headline: CLT-UFA sees 100 bln Luxfr turnover in 1997.

text.p: Luxembourg-based broadcasting group CLT-UFA said on Tuesday it expected a turnover of 100 billion Luxembourg francs in 1997 and hoped to earn a profit of five percent of turnover once the newly-founded company is at cruising speed.

"We should have turnover of about 100 billion francs. I cannot give a precise profit forecast but we would be happy to earn five percent of turnover once we're at cruising speed," Remy Sautter, one of CLT-UFA's two chief executive officers, told a news conference.
CLT-UFA is a product of the merger of Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion (CLT) with UFA, the television unit of German media group Bertelsmann.
CLT's shareholders on Monday gave the final go-ahead for the merger.

Bertelsmann and Audiofina signed an agreement to merge their audiovisual units in July, but the deal has taken a long time to get cleared by the boards and shareholders of the complex control structure above CLT.

The company will be managed jointly and equally by Sautter and UFA's Rolf Schmidt-Holtz, with Sautter responsible for all non-German speaking television operations of CLT-UFA and radio and Schmidt-Holtz for German speaking television and international audiovisual rights.
Under the agreement, Audiofina and Bertelsmann will each hold 49 percent in CLT-UFA.
Audiofina is indirectly controlled by Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA (GBL). French Havas has a minority stake.
CLT-UFA will have its headquarters in Luxembourg, where the group's staff operations and main operations will be based.
The company gave up its ambitions in digital pay television in September, but remains one of Europe's top players in free, advertising-funded television.
